style.summary:
style of A: A is hesitant and fragmented, with filler words and repeated false starts, which makes A sound unsure about the plan.
style of B: B is brief and businesslike, confirming the plan in clipped phrases that sound direct and easy.

A: A's request for accommodation makes B the one who adapts to A's terms.
A's contingency about the phone number gives A control over the safety terms of the arrangement.
A's repeated self-corrections draw B into a supportive register that steers the tone toward A.
B: B's brisk confirmations keep the exchange on B's pace and convey authority.
B's offer to wake A up makes the plan B's responsibility and reads as a directive tone.
B's short replies leave A little room to change the terms, so B controls the register.

A: A's request is only resolved by B's offer, so B decides whether A's accommodation is granted.
A's repeated self-corrections signal uncertainty that weakens A's standing, leaving B's steady confirmations to set the tone.
A's phone-number contingency is a condition B can accept or refuse, which leaves B with the final say.
B: B's brevity reflects efficiency, while A's extra details give A the substance that defines the plan.
The wake-up offer is a favour that A depends on, so A keeps leverage by deciding whether the call is needed.
Short replies leave room for A to add conditions, as the phone number shows, so A still shapes the outcome.

content.summary:
content of A: A sets the arrangement for one night, fixing the meeting time and place along with a backup plan.
content of B: B repeats the time and place and adds the wake-up role, confirming the logistics.

A: A proposes the meeting time and place, so the plan starts from A's proposal.
A introduces the backup phone number, which adds a condition that A determines.
A's account of the arrangement keeps the substance of the exchange on A's terms.
B: B repeats the time and place, which fixes the logistics as B has accepted them.
B's wake-up offer turns the logistics into a commitment that B takes on.
B's confirmations of each detail give B the role of verifying the plan.

A: A's proposal only becomes the plan once B confirms it, so B decides what the plan is.
The phone number is a backup that B's offer of a wake-up call makes unnecessary, so B's commitment matters more.
A's account of the arrangement depends on B's acceptance, so B has the final say on the substance.
B: B's repetition of the time and place adds no new decision, and A set the logistics in the first place.
The wake-up offer is conditional on A's need, so A's request is what shapes B's commitment.
Verifying details is a passive role that leaves A's proposal intact.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: A holds the floor and makes the proposals, with B confirming at the end of each turn.
coordination of B: B takes short turns that confirm and close each exchange, letting A continue.

A: A holds the floor for the longest stretch and sets the agenda for the exchange.
A raises the backup plan in a long turn, which gives A the chance to frame the next steps.
A's repeated restarts keep the floor, so A decides when B can speak.
B: B's short closing turns end each topic, which gives B the last word on each exchange.
B's offer to wake A up is a turn that moves the plan forward without A needing to ask.
B's confirmations let B set the pace of the exchange.

A: A's floor-holding exists only because B allows A to speak, so B controls the turns.
A's long turn is an uncertain request that B can answer briefly and redirect.
A's restarts show A losing the thread, which leaves B to steer the exchange.
B: B's closing turns are brief confirmations, so they do not decide the agenda that A has set.
The wake-up offer answers A's worry, so it is a response to A rather than a lead.
B's confirmations follow A's pace, which means A still sets the tempo.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: A shows concern about punctuality and builds a safety net, which signals investment in the arrangement.
engagement of B: B responds with a single proactive offer that takes on responsibility for the plan.

A: A's concern about being on time signals investment that gives A the greater stake.
A's offer of a fallback phone number shows A's commitment to the arrangement's success.
A's care for the outcome prompts B to offer help, which puts A in the position to receive it.
B: B's offer to wake A up is a proactive gesture that puts B in the role of problem-solver.
B's single offer resolves A's worry, so B controls how the problem is handled.
B's willingness to take on responsibility gives B authority over the plan.

A: A's concern for the outcome is a sign of dependence, which leaves B holding the solution.
A's fallback is a precaution that only matters if B's wake-up call fails, so B is the decisive party.
A's care prompts B's offer, but B decides whether to make it, so B holds the decision.
B: B's offer is a single turn that answers A's worry, so it reflects A's need rather than B's initiative.
B's resolution depends on A's request, so A controls the problem B handles.
B's responsibility is a commitment that A can hold B to, which gives A the leverage.
